finding.summary: `Arguments.iterate` now skips blank cells inside *every* range (not just unbounded ones), changing the result of all existing bounded-range aggregations, but the diff adds no test for that change — and MIN/MAX over a range with no numeric cells is untested and regresses.
finding.evidence: packages/sheets/src/formula/arguments.ts (diff): `const isRange = isSrng(node.v); ... if (!cell || cell.v === undefined || cell.v === '') continue;` applies to any range, e.g. `=MIN(A1:A3)`/`=MAX(A1:A3)`/`=AVERAGE(A1:A3)` on a pre-existing bounded range. The only tests touching this are indirect (`=AVERAGE(B2:B)`→200, `=COUNT(A:B)`→5 in test/sheet/calculation.test.ts, and COUNT does not even use `iterate`). Searching the whole test suite for MIN/MAX over a grid range finds only literal-argument tests (test/formula/formula.test.ts:519-529). Consequently `minFunc`/`maxFunc` (src/formula/functions-statistical.ts:85-98, 110-123) leak their `Infinity`/`-Infinity` accumulator once blanks are skipped — the later main I could read contains exactly that fix plus new tests (`describe('Aggregations over ranges with no numeric cells')`, formula.test.ts:4412-4438) that are NOT in this diff, i.e. the regression shipped uncaught because this change has no direct test.
